title: KS-969 round-1 gate residue: the pre-suite step and its own test suite — six items on one path
description:
## BLUF

Six findings from the **#892 / KS-969 item 1 round-1 tier-2 gate**, left open after round 2 closed
F1 (BLOCKER), F2 and F3. **One ticket, six items** (Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule). **No round 3 —**
**Wednesday spent the cap deliberately**, so these are scheduled work, not a gate on #892.

Two of them (**items 3, 4, 5**) are defects in **the suite I wrote**, not in the product. Recorded
as plainly as the rest.

## SEARCHED BEFORE FILING

SYMBOL `runPreSuiteStep`, `provisionActors`, `writeRejectedManifest`, `ALLOW_REMOTE_PROVISION`,
`_run_pre_suite` · PATH `pre-suite`, `pre_suite.test.sh`, `actor_manifest` · STRING "pre-suite",
"PROVISIONED", "unredacted", "seeded actors". Only **KS-969** (parent) and **KS-966** match.

---

## ITEM 1 (MAJOR, was F4) — akto's provisioning creates actors akto cannot read

`playwright/config/actorManifest.ts`, `performance/runner/actor_manifest.ts` and
`schemathesis/tests/actor_manifest.py` all exist and are imported by live code. **akto has no**
**manifest consumer at all** — no `actorManifest`, no `generated/actors`. Its Secuura credentials come
from `config/secrets.yml` (`.env.example:40`).

So every akto run performs a real **account-creating** provisioning pass whose output akto never
reads, then prints `PROVISIONED — 5 generated actor(s)`. Under this PR's own vocabulary
(`pre-suite.ts:17`, *"the manifest is written; suites read generated actors"*) **that banner is false**
**for akto** — on the suite whose whole job is BOLA/BFLA role enforcement, a reader is told the wrong
identity was under test.

May be deliberate staging for KS-969 item 4. **Decide: either give akto a manifest consumer, or do**
**not hook it and say why.** A green banner asserting something untrue today is the worse of the two.

## ITEM 2 (MAJOR, was F5) — the schemathesis DEGRADED banner never reaches the run record

`_run_pre_suite` uses `subprocess.run` with inherited fds while `Logger` writes the archived log
itself. Measured with `--enable-logger-file`: **pre-suite lines in the archived log = 0.**
On the fatal path the log at least records `Pre-suite provisioning step failed`; on the **DEGRADED**
path `pre_rc == 0`, so nothing is logged and **the archived artefact contains no record that the scan**
**ran on seeded accounts** — the entire point of the banner. The silent fallback, relocated into the
artefact layer.
**Fix-shape:** capture the child's output and re-emit through `Logger`, or log the outcome
unconditionally rather than only on non-zero.

## ITEM 3 (MINOR, was F6) — `pre_suite.test.sh` mutates a shared stack and clobbers the real manifest

Run against any stack answering on `localhost:6882`, the suite **creates five real accounts** with
`FIXTURE_SEED="presuite-test-$$"` — **a fresh seed every run**, so they accumulate and are never
cleaned up — and **overwrites** `systemTest/fixtures/generated/actors.json`, leaving every consumer
pointed at throwaway identities until someone re-provisions.
**This is confirmed by consequence:** the author exhausted the local register limiter (100/hour)
during development, which is exactly this defect compounding. Round 2 partly mitigates it (a role
collapse no longer publishes the manifest), **but the account creation is unchanged.**
**Fix-shape:** a stable seed, and gate the live arm behind an explicit opt-in rather than "a stack
answered".

## ITEM 4 (MINOR, was F7) — the `ALLOW_REMOTE_PROVISION` control is inert and its comment is wrong

`pre_suite.test.sh` comments a cell *"the SAME remote target with the documented override must NOT*
*refuse"* — but it targets `http://127.0.0.1:1`, a **local** host, so it passes through the
`LOCAL_HOSTS` branch and the override is never exercised. Proved by tamper: making the override
branch permanently unreachable still left the suite fully green. **The documented escape hatch is**
**untested in both directions.** The cell still does the job of proving the step does not refuse
everything — so this is a weakened control plus a misleading comment, not an absent one.

## ITEM 5 (MINOR, was F8) — the DEGRADED stream routing is documented and pinned by nothing

`pre-suite.ts` routes DEGRADED to stderr with a comment explaining why. Collapsing both branches to
`console.log` left the suite green, because the harness merges the streams with `2>&1`. **A**
**documented invariant with no test is a comment.**

## ITEM 6 (MINOR, was F9) — unredacted server-error passthrough, PREMISE UNVERIFIED

`provision.ts:282` interpolates the server's `error.message` verbatim into the Error, and
`pre-suite.ts` interpolates that into the DEGRADED banner. Against a stub that echoes the request
body, **the generated password appeared in the banner in cleartext.**
**The gate proved the pipe is unredacted; it did NOT prove the real endpoint echoes payloads** — it
never reached a real stack. **Recorded with the premise unverified rather than smoothed over.** Value
at risk is low (generated `.invalid` local accounts); fix-shape is trivial — redact `password` keys
before interpolation.

## PROVENANCE

QA tier-2 gate on **#892 @** `f54b2dce1`, reported 2026-09-07. F1/F2/F3 closed in round 2 at
`42e778203`. Wednesday ruled **no round 3**, so these ship as their own work.

nodes.title: KS-973: the pre-suite step redacts the generated password, pins its DEGRADED stream, drives its second quarantine call — items 5, 6 + two residues; items 3/4 wait for #927; items 1/2 are L11/L12 files

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 989 merged as a9ce2cff1594 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (recorded deploy, 2026-11-01). Verified by code read at b1fb543640e7, not observed live (test tooling under `systemTest/`). Left open: items 1 to 4, as the ticket's last comment records them.

- **Items 5 and 6 and the two round-5 residues are in the code:** `systemTest/fixtures/provision.ts:271` defines `redactSecrets(text, secrets)` and :338 applies it where the server's message is interpolated into the Error that `pre-suite.ts` prints as the DEGRADED banner; the squash adds `provisionRedaction.test.ts`, `preSuiteStreams.test.ts` and `provisionDriftQuarantine.test.ts` under `systemTest/performance/tests/unit/fixtures/`.
- **Left open, as comment dc2e29c8 of 2026-09-14 records it (not re-checked here):** items 3 and 4 waited on PR 927, and items 1 and 2 were other lanes' files.

**PR #989 is READY FOR QA at `e62fd23cda1bc120716e5f592efac2b8abea97bf` (tier 1, DELTA re-gate, round 2) — 2026-09-14, s232. This ticket STAYS In Progress: items 3/4 wait on #927 (open at `1041d2d32`); items 1/2 are other lanes' files.**

**What round 2 changed, and why.** The tier-1 gate on `9d0e2016a` (GO WITH FINDINGS, 09:17Z) found F-1: round 1 carried an undisclosed whole-file prettier reformat of `systemTest/fixtures/provision.ts` and `pre-suite.ts` (+795 −276 against the body's "+332 −1"), semantics proven preserved — the residual over M38's blobs was exactly the three intended hunks. `systemTest/fixtures/` has no formatter config, and develop's `4dcc992b7` undid this same class on `provision-actors.ts` on 2026-09-10. Round 2 follows that precedent: both files restored from M38's blobs (`b95f4ee39` / `01024fadd`), the three hunks re-applied by hand in the files' own 4-space / single-quote style — the `redactSecrets` docblock + function; the four-line item-6 comment + the one redacted interpolation site; the four-line residue-(e) comment above `invokedDirectly` — as ONE new commit `e62fd23cd` on top of `9d0e2016a` (never a rewrite), after `develop` `311988614` was merged in `--no-ff`. New fixture blobs `cff58deaa` / `c3846e272`; the three cell files byte-unchanged (`1e384fb1d` / `2de77e9db` / `2cc4be3d6`). True numstat against develop: `4 0` · `30 1` · `106 0` · `154 0` · `203 0` (+497 −1), plain and `-w` identical.

**Measured at the merged head:** `prettier --check` over the eight fixture files fails exactly M38's five (`provision.ts`, `pre-suite.ts`, `actors.ts`, `manifest.ts`, `provision-actors.ts`) — round 1's head showed 3; the directory's style split is back where develop has it. `tsc --noEmit -p fixtures/tsconfig.json` rc 0 (plant control: a `const x: number = 'y'` in a scratch copy → `TS2322`, rc 2). `npm run typecheck` from `systemTest/` rc 0 (seven configs, 0 `error TS`). `tests/unit/fixtures/` 11 files / 260; the three new files 9 / 9; the whole performance unit suite 61 files / 1056 before and after the restore. `npm run lint` rc 0. Tamper T2 (the interpolation site put back to raw) → exactly 2 red in `provisionRedaction.test.ts`, restored by content (`hash-object` = `cff58deaa`), 5 / 5 again. Push fast-forward, push-protocol PROTOCOL-CLEAN; the hook ran the systemTest format gate (OK) and no 15-leg preflight for this `systemTest/`-only range.

**Not run:** live provisioning (a stack is on hold — item 6's premise, a real endpoint echoing payloads, is still unverified by design); the four platform suites; items 3/4 (#927's file); items 1/2; the gate's eight tampers beyond the one re-run here.

**Two records from the gate, carried here as facts (Wednesday's routing: this ticket, the PR's own; a board search for `buildPassword` returned 0 issues and `redactSecrets` only the Playwright-coverage ticket — no prior record):**
- **R-1 (the gate's G7):** for the five deterministic actors (owner, issuer, approver, verifier, orgAdmin) the DEGRADED banner still carries `spec.key` and `spec.email`, which are the two inputs of `buildPassword(key, seed)` (`systemTest/fixtures/actors.ts:91-97`: `Ks256-${key}-${seed}-Pw!`; the seed is parseable from the `ks256-<key>-<seed>` local part of the `.invalid` address) — so the redacted password of a `.invalid` test account on a local stack is reconstructible from the thrown message. A property of KS-256's deterministic actors, recorded here; not a defect of this PR, whose item-6 fix-shape (redact the password before interpolation) is delivered exactly.
- **R-2:** `redactSecrets` boundaries measured by the gate: order-dependent with overlapping secrets (unreachable — one secret per call); exact-substring only — a JSON-escaped or case-changed echo is not redacted (unreachable for the generated alphabet; reachable only for a hand-typed `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, which is never interpolated).

**For the merge seat:** the delta for the gate is `git diff -w 0e78c7270 <head> -- systemTest/fixtures/` = the three hunks (plain = `-w`); equality targets are the two new fixture blobs `cff58deaa` / `c3846e272` + the three unchanged cells. The branch key `ks-973` will make the integration try to move this ticket at the squash — it must be restored to In Progress: items 3/4 are not started and wait on #927.

## PR #989 — READY FOR QA (tier 1, round 1) — items 5, 6 + the two round-5 residues built; items 3/4 wait for #927; items 1/2 recorded (s227, 2026-09-14). THE TICKET STAYS OPEN.

**BLUF.** https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/989 at **`9d0e2016ae60658ec908ee5e500583fd3a318c8a`** (`git ls-remote` 07:21:54Z; first push, push-protocol CLEAN), on develop M38 `0e78c7270`; 5 files, +332 −1, two commits. Tier 1 as ruled by Wednesday: the redaction reaches every suite's pre-suite error path — a secret-handling surface.

**Built here:** item 6 — `redactSecrets(text, secrets)` in `provision.ts`, applied at the ONE site that interpolates a server message (the throw at the end of `provisionActor`, with the actor's password; `login`/`createAsAdmin`/`bootstrapToken` return null and interpolate nothing). **The premise that a real endpoint echoes payloads stays UNVERIFIED** — no stack was reached; the pipe is redacted regardless. Item 5 — the DEGRADED-to-stderr routing pinned by a cell that spawns the real `pre-suite.ts` against `127.0.0.1:1` and reads the streams apart. Residue (comment `a55ab963` §1) — `provision-actors.ts`' drift-arm `quarantineManifest` call is driven end-to-end with a stubbed `fetch` and the REAL rename aimed at a temp target: a pre-created manifest is superseded, nothing published; the F1-spec negative control holds. Residue (§2) — the symlink shape of `invokedDirectly` pinned as KNOWN (exit 0, empty output) + a comment at the site; not fixed.

**Evidence:** red-first on develop's `provision.ts` 4 failed / 5 passed — two assertion reds show the generated password in the thrown message AND in the DEGRADED banner (the gate's measured shape); 9/9 after. Tampers: the CLI tail collapsed to `console.log` reds exactly the streams cell; the redaction call reverted reds exactly the two password cells. Whole `performance` unit suite **59 files / 1051 tests** (baseline 56 / 1042); lint 0/0, knip 0, `format:check` rc 0, KS-989 gate OK. `fixtures/generated/` absent before and after in the worktree — every cell uses its own temp dir.

**Not built, by partition:** item 1 lives in `systemTest/akto/tests/preSuiteSetup.ts` / `akto/src/**` (L12); item 2 in `systemTest/schemathesis/scripts/run.py:353-391` (L11). **Not started:** items 3/4 edit `systemTest/__tests__/pre_suite.test.sh`, which PR #927 (`1041d2d32`, open, unmerged at 07:21:40Z) holds — they begin only on a develop that contains #927's merge. **This ticket does not close on #989.**

## Two items from the #892 round-5 gate that belong here, NOT in round 5

Round 5 was bounded to F-1 and F-2 by Kam's word ("F-1 and F-2 only, F-2 first"), so neither of these was touched. Recording them so they are not mistaken for tested.

### 1. A SECOND unguarded `quarantineManifest` call — `provision-actors.ts:178`

Round 5's F-1 fix wrapped the call at `pre-suite.ts:157`. **There is another one at `provision-actors.ts:178`, and it was NOT driven by any cell.**

**It cannot break the same contract** — it sits inside `runPreSuite`'s own `try`, so a throw there is caught and classified. **But it is untested**, and "covered by an outer try" is a structural argument, not a measurement. If the F-3 work touches this path, drive it.

### 2. `invokedDirectly` can silently exit 0 through a symlinked path (F5-3, curio)

`pre-suite.ts` decides whether it was run directly by comparing a **realpath'd** `import.meta.url` against an **unresolved** `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1])`. Invoked through a symlink the two differ, `invokedDirectly` is false, the CLI body never runs — and the process **exits 0 having done nothing**.

**Correctly bounded and NOT a live defect:** all four production hooks resolve real paths before invoking it, so this is reachable only by manual invocation through a symlink. Recorded because a silent exit 0 is the shape that gets mistaken for success.

Both from the tier-2 gate on #892 round 5 (GO with findings; neither is gating). #892 is merged — `develop` `512480ef1`.

**UPDATE to item 3 — its severity note is now out of date, and in the direction that understates it.**

Item 3 currently credits a round-2 mitigation:

> *"Round 2 partly mitigates it (a role collapse no longer publishes the manifest), **but the account creation is unchanged**."*

**Round 3 and round 4 have replaced that mitigation with an ACTIVE MUTATION.** A role collapse no longer merely declines to publish — it now **moves an existing `generated/actors.json` aside** to `actors.superseded-<stamp>.json` (round 3), and as of round 4 a provisioning **throw** does the same from `runPreSuite`'s catch.

`pre_suite.test.sh` runs the real step against any stack answering on `:6882` with a fresh `presuite-test-$$` seed. So each run of that suite now:

1. creates five real accounts (unchanged — the original finding), **and**
2. **moves the real manifest aside**, leaving every consumer with no manifest until someone re-provisions.

**(2) is new.** The mitigation the severity note credits is gone, replaced by something with a larger footprint. That is not an argument against the quarantine — the quarantine is correct and was commissioned — it is an argument that **this item got more urgent, not less**, and the note should not be read as reassurance.

**Fix-shape is unchanged** (a stable seed, and gate the live arm behind an explicit opt-in rather than "a stack answered"), but the opt-in gate now matters for a second reason: an accidental run no longer just adds accounts, it also removes the manifest the other suites depend on.

**Not filed as a new ticket** — it is the same defect and the same fix, and this board's rule is one ticket per logical path with items inside.

*Source: #892 round-3 QA gate finding F1-C, 2026-09-07T10:49:17Z. Verified against `1e31c80b9`: the quarantine call is live in both `provision-actors.ts`' drift arm and `pre-suite.ts`' catch arm.*

# F1 fix-shape — specification, written while the ticket is HELD

**BLUF — the F1 fix must handle a manifest that ALREADY EXISTS on disk, not merely decline to write a new one. A live instance is present right now on `worktrees/seat-a`, and it is the exact shape the round-2 fix does not cover.**

No code and no branches were touched to write this: `#892` is carded to Kam for a possible narrow round 3, and KS-973's files are `#892`'s files. This is a specification so that round starts from a written defect rather than a memory.

## The claim in the code that is not true

`provision-actors.ts:154-156` states the mechanism in its own words:

> *"when we cannot keep the promise we do not make it: the manifest is NOT published, every consumer falls back to its seeded accounts **because the file simply is not there**, and the rejected copy goes to a sidecar for diagnosis."*

**"Because the file simply is not there" is an assumption about the filesystem, not a property the code establishes.** `writeRejectedManifest` writes `generated/actors.rejected.json`; nothing touches `generated/actors.json`. A **non-write is not a removal.** If a previous run already published a manifest, it survives the rejection and every consumer reads it — believing it current.

## The live instance, on `worktrees/seat-a` at `42e778203`

Metadata only; no credentials or actor bodies read out:

| file | seed | provisionedAt |
|---|---|---|
| `generated/actors.json` | `presuite-test-72460` | **2026-09-07T07:57:14Z** |
| `generated/actors.rejected.json` | `presuite-strict-47722` | **2026-09-07T08:50:37Z** |

The rejected run is **53 minutes newer** than the published manifest. So the most recent provisioning pass was refused, and the file the three consumers resolve is still the **07:57** one. The fallback the comment promises did not happen, because the file was there.

**`generated/` is gitignored** (`systemTest/fixtures/.gitignore:8`), which is why this persists silently across runs and never shows up in `git status`. A clean working tree is not evidence the manifest is clean.

## It compounds with item 3 of this ticket, and that is the worse half

The surviving manifest's seed is **`presuite-test-72460`** — the `presuite-test-$$` shape that **item 3** records `pre_suite.test.sh` writing into the real manifest path. So the two defects interlock:

1. **item 3** puts throwaway test identities into `generated/actors.json`;
2. **F1** then declines to overwrite it on a rejected run and leaves them standing.

The consumers on that worktree are currently pointed at accounts a test suite created for itself. Fixing either one alone leaves the pairing live.

## Fix-shape

**Quarantine the stale manifest on rejection — do not merely skip the write.** On the `drifted.length > 0` path, if `MANIFEST_PATH` exists, move it aside (e.g. `actors.superseded-<provisionedAt>.json`) *before* returning, then write the rejected sidecar as now. **Move, never delete** — the standing rule, and the superseded file is the diagnostic record of what the suites *would* have run on.

**Why quarantine rather than a reader-side freshness check.** `manifest.ts` argues that the guard living in the FILE rather than in a reader is load-bearing, because `schemathesis/tests/actor_manifest.py` parses the JSON directly and a TypeScript-side check would never cover it. That argument is correct and it applies here too: a `provisionedAt`/`seed`/`baseUrl` staleness check would have to be implemented in **both** languages across **three** consumers, and any consumer that forgot it would silently keep the old behaviour. Making the filesystem state true is one change in one place and cannot be forgotten by a consumer.

**The no-stale-manifest case must not change.** When no manifest exists, the current non-write is already correct, and the fix must not start creating or removing anything there.

## What a test must pin, and how it can fail

Two cells, and the second is the one that makes the first mean anything:

1. **Pre-create a manifest, then provision with a drifted role.** Assert `MANIFEST_PATH` no longer resolves to the pre-created content, and that a superseded copy exists. *Red-proof:* with only the round-2 fix in place this cell fails, because the stale file is still there and still readable.
2. **Negative / positive control — provision with NO pre-existing manifest and a drifted role.** Assert nothing is quarantined and no manifest is published. Without this, a fix that unconditionally deleted or wrote something would pass cell 1.

A cell asserting only *"`writeManifest` was not called"* is the check that cannot fail here — it is true today, on the very worktree that carries the live instance.

## Also correct the comment

`provision-actors.ts:154-156` must stop asserting *"the file simply is not there"* once the behaviour changes — and if round 3 is not authorised, it should stop asserting it anyway, because it is the load-bearing sentence a reader would rely on and it is false. Same class as the `documentRepo` comment corrected on KS-597 today: a comment that describes a property the code does not have.
